outcome: perinatal outcomes (e.g., gestational age at delivery, birth weight, incidence of multiple pregnancies, length of hospital stay post-delivery, mode of delivery)
neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission rates (secondary-level NICU)
neonatal immunization rates (Hepatitis B vaccination, Vitamin K administration)
cohort: A total of 10,560 pregnant women (10,407 Turkish citizens and 158 Syrian immigrants) who received care at a tertiary referral center between June 2020 and June 2025.
finding: While overall perinatal outcomes were comparable between Syrian immigrant and Turkish citizen pregnant women, neonates born to Syrian immigrant mothers had a higher rate of secondary-level NICU admission compared to Turkish citizens.
mod_finding: The overall cesarean section rate was 67.2% for Turkish women and 56.3% for Syrian women, making it the most common mode of delivery overall.
gest_age: Overall mean: 38 weeks (Turkish: 38 weeks; Syrian: 39 weeks)
